facts.statement: The genus Embaphias was named by Edward Drinker Cope based on three cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: It was named by Edward Drinker Cope on the basis of three cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: Three incomplete plesiosaur vertebrae were collected in 1893 by John H. Charles from the Pierre Formation in Great Bend of the Missouri River, South Dakota.
facts.quote: In 1893, John H. Charles, a man from Sioux City, collected three incomplete plesiosaur vertebrae from strata of the Pierre Formation in Great Bend of the Missouri River, South Dakota.

facts.statement: Edward Drinker Cope described the fossils as a new genus and species, Embaphias circulosus, in 1894.
facts.quote: In 1894, American paleontologist Edward Drinker Cope described these vertebrae as coming from a new genus and species of plesiosaur, Embaphias circulosus.

facts.statement: The generic name Embaphias is derived from the Greek word for 'saucer'.
facts.quote: The generic name Embaphias derives from the Greek word embaphion, "saucer", and -ias , a suffix for Greek words.

facts.statement: The specific name circulosus comes from the Latin word for 'circle' or 'ring'.
facts.quote: The specific name comes from the Latin word circulus, "circle" or "ring".

facts.statement: Cope identified one vertebra as cervical and the other two as dorsal.
facts.quote: Cope identified one of these vertebrae as a cervical (neck) vertebra and the other two as being dorsal (back) vertebrae.

facts.statement: The genus is known only from three incomplete vertebrae, one cervical and two dorsal.
facts.quote: Embaphias is only represented by three incomplete vertebrae (one cervical and two dorsals).

facts.statement: The cervical vertebra is flattened front-to-back and has a circular outline.
facts.quote: The cervical is flattened anterioposteriorly and is overall circular in outline.

facts.statement: A large vascular foramen is located below the articular rim of the cervical centrum.
facts.quote: A large vascular foramen (an opening of bone where blood would flow) is located below the articular rim (area where the centrum would articulate with another centrum) of the cervical centrum.

facts.statement: The cervical centrum measures 84 mm in transverse diameter, 78 mm in vertical diameter, and 45 mm in side length.
facts.quote: The cervical centrum has a transverse diameter of 84 mm, vertical diameter of 78 mm, and a side length of 45 mm.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebra has a pair of moderately developed diapophyses on its lateral sides that point vertically.
facts.quote: On the lateral sides of the cervical central are a pair of diapophyses that are moderately developed and point vertically.

facts.statement: Embaphias lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) period.
Embaphias is a dubious genus of plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America.
facts.quote: Embaphias is a dubious genus of plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America.

facts.statement: Embaphias is classified as a dubious genus of plesiosaur.
facts.quote: Embaphias is a dubious genus of plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America.

facts.statement: The parent group of Embaphias is Plesiosauria.
Embaphias belongs to the class Reptilia.
Williston and Moodie (1917) suggested the fossils belong to its own genus based on the age and concavity of the vertebrae.
facts.quote: However its age and the concavity of the anterior-posterior faces of the cervical and dorsal centra led Williston and Moodie (1917) to suggest it comes from its own genus.
